newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch NAM makes "promising" offshore gas find.
newsitem.headline: Dutch NAM makes "promising" offshore gas find.

text.p: Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM) -- a 50/50 Dutch joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon -- said on Wednesday it had made a promising gas discovery in the Wadden Sea, part of the North Sea off the north coast of the Netherlands.

"We can't say how large the discovery is, but it looks like a promising find. We don't always say that," said NAM spokesman Frank Duut. NAM will conduct a series of tests and hopes to establish the size of the find by next spring.
Gasunie, the Dutch monopoly gas supplier, said the minimum expectation was of a 200 billion cubic metre field.
"And there's a feeling it could be at least 50 percent larger than that," Gasunie spokesman Abraham Warner said.
The borehole, in the North Friesland concession and initially drilled this spring, is three km offshore and reaches a depth of four km, NAM said.
"In total (the hole) is about six km, which is quite a long hole for NAM," said Duut.
The concession is 40 percent owned by NAM, 40 percent by Mobil Producing Netherlands and 20 percent by Energie Beheer Nederland, a Dutch state agency.
NAM is investigating over 10 sites in the Wadden Sea and expects further discoveries.

"We're still not at the end of the road, although the major finds (in the Netherlands) are behind us. Government policy is helping people to explore as much as they can," Duut said. --Philip Blenkinsop, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
